\begin{abstract}
Luminal breast cancers differ in outcome. We trained 33 models on 4,329 samples
and found 14 genes shared between observed and predicted sets \cite{curtis2012}.
\end{abstract}

\noindent\textbf{Keywords:} breast cancer; DNA methylation; machine learning; luminal subtypes; epigenetics

\section{Introduction}
Breast cancer has distinct molecular subtypes \citep{johnson2021,curtis2012}. % reviewer asked for this
Luminal tumors account for \textbf{60\%} of cases.
